newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LEMIEUX FIRST TO 100 POINTS AS PENGUINS WIN.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LEMIEUX FIRST TO 100 POINTS AS PENGUINS WIN.

text.p: Superstar centre Mario Lemieux, in the midst of what may be the final campaign of his brilliant NHL career, Saturday became the first player in the league to reach the 100-point mark this season.
Lemieux set up the tying goal to reach the century mark and Fredrik Olausson scored 19 seconds into overtime to lift the Pittsburgh Penguins to a 3-2 win over the Philadelphia Flyers.
With the Penguins on a powerplay trailing 2-1, Lemieux took a slap shot and Glen Murray tipped it into the Flyers net with 7:21 left in regulation.
The assist was Lemieux's 56th -- to go along with 44 goals -- marking the 10th season Super Mario he has reached triple digits in scoring.
In the opening seconds of overtime, Ron Francis found a wide open Olausson at the top of the slot and he sent a wrist shot over Garth Snow's glove, ending Pittsburgh's six-game losing streak.
"It's pretty good to win in overtime against a pretty good team," Lemieux said of Pittsburgh's first overtime win of the season. "I thought we played pretty solid defensively."
Pittsburgh goalie Ken Wregget made 32 saves to break a personal four-game losing streak, while Philadelphia suffered its first loss in 13 overtime contests this season.
In Chicago, Nikolai Khabibulin made 28 saves to post his third consecutive shutout and sixth of the season and Keith Tkachuk scored his 38th goal as the Phoenix Coyotes blanked the Blackhawks 2-0.
Khabibulin established franchise records for shutouts in a season and length of time without surrendering a goal, which he extended to 198 minutes and 19 seconds.
Former Blackhawk Mike Stapleton scored the other goal as Phoenix moved within one point of fourth-place Edmonton in the Western Conference.
In Montreal, Valeri Bure scored a powerplay goal with 2:18 left in regulation as the Canadiens rallied from a 3-1 deficit to forge a 3-3 tie with the Buffalo Sabres.

Despite giving up the tying goal late in the third, Buffalo goaltender Dominik Hasek stopped Vincent Damphousse on a penalty shot and came sliding out to the blue line to foil a late breakaway by Marc Bureau to preserve the tie.
Alexei Zhitnik, Jason Dawe and Barrie Moore scored for Buffalo, while Hasek finished with 40 saves.
Damphousse and Turner Stevenson scored the other Montreal goals.
In Toronto, Robert Kron beat Felix Potvin with 5:08 left in the third period to lift the Hartford Whalers into a 1-1 tie with the Maple Leafs.

The Whalers were coming off back-to-back shutouts and Sean Burke had not allowed a goal for 147 minutes, 38 seconds when Wendel Clark gave Toronto a 1-0 lead at 9:40 of the first period. Burke faced just 17 shots, stopping 16.
Potvin turned aside 34 shots for Toronto, which has a season-high four-game unbeaten streak (2-0-2) going.
At Tampa Bay, Kyle McLaren snapped a 4-4 tie with 8:10 left in the third period as the Boston Bruins rallied from a three-goal deficit for a 6-4 victory over the Lightning.
The Bruins allowed three powerplay goals in the first period, falling behind 4-1 by the first intermission.
Jim Carey replaced Rob Tallas in the Boston goal and stopped all 20 shots he saw over the final two periods.
Anson Carter, who had a short-handed tally early in the first period, scored the first of five unanswered Bruins goals midway through the second to spark the comeback.
On Long Island, Bryan Smolinski had a goal and two assists and Tommy Salo stopped 28 shots as the New York Islanders ended the New Jersey Devils' five-game winning streak with a 5-1 victory.
Zigmund Palffy added a goal and an assist and Travis Green picked up a pair of assists for the Islanders, who climbed within three points of an Eastern Conference playoff spot.
The Devils played without injured centre Doug Gilmour, whose acquisition from Toronto coincided with the team's winning streak.
In Los Angeles, Byron Dafoe made 44 saves and Ian Laperriere scored twice to lead the Kings to a 3-1 win over the Ottawa Senators.
Ray Ferraro scored the other goal for Los Angeles, which won for the sixth time in eight games.
Daniel Alfredsson spoiled Dafoe's shutout bid, scoring Ottawa's lone goal on a powerplay at 13:37 of the second.
In Vancouver, Brendan Shanahan scored his 42nd goal and set up another in a three-goal second period as the Detroit Red Wings built a 4-0 lead and held on for a 5-3 win over the Canucks.
Martin Lapointe, Tomas Holmstrom, Igor Larionov and Nicklas Lidstrom also scored for Detroit, which ran its unbeaten streak to 10 games 6-0-4.
Scott Walker, Esa Tikkanen and Markus Naslund scored for Vancouver.
